cards.q: Exam 18 Jan 2019 · Q 1.11. Let us assume that you have to model the term structure of interest rates of a given country or currency.Please explain the type of information usually employed and their main pros and cons. (1)
cards.a:
• Spot, forward or discount rates from zero-coupon bonds
  • Usually there are not enough zero-coupon bonds => prices/yields of coupon-paying bonds are used and the yield curve is estimates/smoothed afterwards
  • For the short-term, there are usually zero-coupon govt bonds (Treasury bills). cards.q: Exam 5 Jan 2024 · Q 2.22. cards.a:
DNSS:

$$s_{t,m}=\beta_{0,t}+\beta_{1,t}\cdot\left[1-e^{(-\lambda_{1t}m)}\right]/(\lambda_{1t}m)$$
$$+\beta_2\cdot\left\{\left[1-e^{(-\lambda_{1t}m)}\right]/(\lambda_{1t}m)-e^{(-\lambda_{1t}m)}\right\}$$
$$+\beta_3\cdot\left\{\left[1-e^{(-\lambda_{2t}m)}\right]/(\lambda_{2t}m)-e^{(-\lambda_{2t}m)}\right\}$$
  • the NS model is a restricted version of the Svensson model with the restriction b3 = 0 and/or t2→ 0. Thus, we can test the null hypothesis corresponding to those restrictions:
$$H_0:\ \beta_0=\beta_1=\ldots=\beta_q=0$$
  • The test is based on the following log-likelihood ratio test:
$$-2\left(\ln v-\ln v^*\right)\sim\chi^2(q)$$

where: v = likelihood function of the adjustment with restrictions; v* = likelihood function of the adjustment without restrictions; q = number of restrictions.

Maximum Likelihood Estimation Problem. (The test statistic and the ML problem are tiny images in the correction; the statistic above is written from the slides.)
